title: A TLS point cloud dataset with detailed annotations for leaf-on and leaf-off seasons across multiple tree species - HuashuTrees
abstract: Terrestrial laser scanning (TLS) captures accurate 3D tree geometry, benefiting forest management and ecology. Deep learning has enhanced TLS point cloud processing but requires extensive training data with semantic annotations. Existing datasets typically focus on tree segmentation or species classification, lacking detailed leaf-wood separation, which is essential for carbon stock and photosynthesis modelling. Real-world TLS data with leaf-wood labels remain scarce, come from limited regions (e.g., Cameroon, Finland, USA, India), and are mostly leaf-on only. To fill this gap, we introduce HuashuTrees, a public multi-species bi-seasonal TLS dataset from deciduous broadleaf forests in Nanjing, China (leaf-off: January 2025; leaf-on: July 2025). Other than plot-level point clouds, it includes 318 single-tree point clouds from 159 trees across seven species, generated after registration, denoising, segmentation, leaf-wood separation, and manual correction. Technical validation confirms high consistency for leaf-wood annotation, with a mean agreement of 96.34% between the final dataset labels and independent manual re-classification. Additionally, TLS-derived diameter at breast height (DBH) shows strong agreement with field measurements (RMSE = 0.356 cm, R² = 0.978). HuashuTrees supports algorithm development for leaf-wood separation, segmentation, species classification, structure inversion, 3D reconstruction, and multi-temporal monitoring.

title: A multi-task video reasoning dataset across semantic, spatial, and temporal categories with four difficulty levels
abstract: Visual reasoning, the capability to interpret visual input in response to implicit text query through multi-step reasoning, remains a challenge for deep learning models due to the lack of relevant benchmarks. Previous work in visual reasoning has primarily focused on reasoning segmentation, where models aim to segment objects based on implicit text queries. This paper introduces reasoning visual tasks (RVTs), a unified formulation that extends beyond traditional video reasoning segmentation to a diverse family of visual language reasoning problems, which can therefore accommodate multiple output formats including bounding boxes, natural language descriptions, and question-answer pairs. Correspondingly, we identify the limitations in current benchmark construction methods that rely solely on large language models (LLMs), which inadequately capture complex spatial-temporal relationships and multi-step reasoning chains in video due to their reliance on token representation, resulting in benchmarks with artificially limited reasoning complexity. To address this limitation, we propose a novel automated RVT benchmark construction pipeline that leverages digital twin (DT) representations as structured intermediaries between perception and the generation of implicit text queries. Based on this method, we construct RVTBench, a RVT benchmark containing 3,896 queries of over 1.2 million tokens across four types of RVT (segmentation, grounding, VQA and summary), three reasoning categories (semantic, spatial, and temporal), and four increasing difficulty levels, derived from 200 video sequences. Finally, we propose RVTagent, an agent framework for RVT that allows for zero-shot generalization across various types of RVT without task-specific fine-tuning. Dataset and code are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19697191 and https://github.com/yiqings/rvt .

title: A Multi-Source Pixel-Level Annotated Dataset for Hemorrhage Recognition in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy
abstract: Intraoperative hemorrhage is a critical safety challenge in laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC) and other minimally invasive surgeries, yet it remains underexplored in surgical artificial intelligence (AI) research due to limited high-quality annotated data. We introduce LC-HemSeg, a multi-source, multi-scene dataset comprising 30 annotated LC cases with 21,396 manually verified frames and pixel-wise hemorrhage annotations. LC-HemSeg captures diverse hemorrhage appearances, with frame-level categories for active bleeding, oozing-type bleeding, blood pooling, and hemorrhage-free scenes. A human-in-the-loop annotation pipeline integrated PoolNet-based pre-segmentation with three-level clinical review by residents, attendings, and experts. The dataset also includes challenging scenes with smoke, motion blur, occlusion, and tissue edema. We provide statistical characterization of hemorrhage burden, frame-level category distributions, inter-case variability, and annotation consistency. LC-HemSeg provides a resource for developing and evaluating hemorrhage segmentation algorithms in LC and may support future research on AI-assisted intraoperative safety systems, pending validation in additional procedures and real-time clinical settings.

title: A human epithelial cell cycle dataset
abstract: We introduce a large-scale single cell dataset for cell cycle phases. The dataset includes single cell images of 4′,6-diamidino-2-phenylindole-stained human epithelioma-2 (HEp-2) cells grown on microscopic glass slides. Greyscale images of adherent HEp-2 cells were acquired at 20x magnification by an automated, inverse microscope system. Cell images were automatically segmented with 256 × 256 pixel patch size including surrounding area. Initially, 10,000 images were manually classified by experts into 5 cell-cycle groups (interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase) and two additional groups (artefact, triple). Based on these initial single cell-image classifications, a convolutional neural network (CNN) model (VGG16) was trained. Subsequently, additional segmented single cell images were pre-classified by the CNN and double-blinded reviewed as well as corrected by two experts to build an algorithm-aided dataset with 100,000 images. The dataset provides a resource for development of biomedical and deep learning applications and, thus, enables training and assessment of cell-cycle detection algorithms.

title: A Multicenter Whole Slide Image Dataset for Classification and Out-of-Distribution Detection in Spindle Cell Cutaneous Neoplasms
abstract: Cutaneous spindle cell (CSC) neoplasms are a notoriously challenging diagnostic group within the spectrum of skin malignancies. While specialized CSC neoplasm datasets like AI4SKIN have enabled the development of AI whole-slide image (WSI) classification methods, these methods are largely constrained by closed-set designs. However, in real-world clinical practice, biopsies often contain secondary tumors or rare entities unknown to the developed AI classifiers. When faced with such Out-of-Distribution (OoD) cases, automated systems can produce highly confident but incorrect predictions, posing a significant risk to patient safety and hindering the reliable deployment of AI in routine pathology. To address this limitation, we present ASSIST, a multicenter dataset of 410 WSIs comprising both spindle-cell tumors and a diverse set of metastatic and rare lesions explicitly included as OoD samples. ASSIST expands AI4SKIN by increasing sample diversity, reinforcing underrepresented categories, and introducing clinically meaningful OoD cases, thereby enabling the development of more robust and safety-oriented computational pathology models. We describe the dataset acquisition pipeline, annotation structure, and technical validation using multiple instance learning (MIL) models combined with a suite of OoD detection methods. ASSIST provides an essential benchmark for advancing open-world pathology and supports future research in dependable AI systems for dermatopathology.

title: Synthetic Production Dataset for Causal Machine Learning in Operations Management
abstract: Causal machine learning represents a promising paradigm for estimating intervention effects in operations management, yet its adoption is constrained by the scarcity of structured datasets suitable for method development and validation. This paper presents a synthetic production dataset comprising 10,000 production order records from a simulated metalworking factory with ten welding lines and ten product types. The dataset incorporates a binary treatment variable representing the implementation of drum-buffer-rope synchronization from the Theory of Constraints on two production lines. Data generation follows established statistical distributions with explicit causal structure, including line-product interaction effects, Little’s Law relationships, and treatment-dependent outcome variations. The dataset includes 15 variables capturing order characteristics, operational parameters, performance outcomes, and a line-level carry-over state that induces temporal serial correlation between successive orders on the same line. Primary reuse value lies in benchmarking causal machine learning methods, particularly meta-learners, tree-based algorithms, and neural network–based approaches for heterogeneous treatment effect estimation in operations management contexts. The dataset supports methodological research on ex-ante effect estimation without requiring explicit simulation models of production systems.

title: Global gapless 1 km daily mean land surface temperature (70°N–60°S, 2003–2023) via integrated approaches
abstract: Land surface temperature (LST) is a fundamental variable in hydrological and climate research. However, cloud contamination and sparse temporal sampling in satellite thermal infrared observations cause extensive data gaps, hindering generation of continuous long-term high-resolution daily mean LSTs. Although global gap-filled and reanalysis-based LST products already exist, they often face one of the challenges: coarse spatial resolutions, monthly mean/daily instantaneous scales, or struggling to balance accuracy and spatial texture. To address these challenges, we integrate empirical, semi-physical, and machine learning approaches to generate gapless 1 km daily mean LSTs for 70°N–60°S and 2003–2023. We implement a pixelwise, daily-mean–then–annual-cycle, preliminary-to-optimized workflow that harmonizes MODIS observations with all-weather in situ measurements. Validation demonstrates progressive accuracy improvements across steps, with final RMSEs of 2.073 K (daily) and 1.511 K (monthly) against independent ground observations. Comparisons with existing gap-filled products and reanalysis datasets demonstrate improved statistical accuracy—particularly over cropland, grassland, and cold regions—as well as enhanced seasonal robustness and spatial texture, particularly over rugged terrain and urban areas.

title: Real-world energy data of 200 feeders from low-voltage grids with metadata in Germany over two years
abstract: The last mile of the distribution grid is crucial for a successful energy transition, as more low-carbon technology like photovoltaic systems, heat pumps, and electric vehicle chargers connect to the low-voltage grid. Despite considerable challenges in operation and planning, researchers often lack access to suitable low-voltage grid data. To address this, we present the FeederBW dataset with data recorded by the German distribution system operator Netze BW. It offers real-world energy data from 200 low-voltage feeders over two years (2023-2025) with weather information and detailed metadata, including changes in low-carbon technology installations. The dataset includes feeder-specific details such as the number of housing units, installed power of low-carbon technology, and aggregated industrial energy data. Furthermore, high photovoltaic feed-in and one-minute temporal resolution makes the dataset unique. FeederBW supports various applications, including machine learning for load forecasting, conducting non-intrusive load monitoring, generating synthetic data, and analyzing the interplay between weather, feeder measurements, and metadata. The dataset reveals insightful patterns and clearly reflects the growing impact of low-carbon technology on low-voltage grids.

title: ROUGE: A database of disaster impacts in the Global South using Red Cross reports and Large Language Models
abstract: High quality data on natural hazard damages are crucial for effective disaster risk management. Yet, existing impact datasets remain limited and often biased toward Northern countries and monetary losses. To help address these gaps, we present ROUGE (Redcross Operations Unified Global Emergency database); a new socio-economic impact database obtained using textual operational reports from the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. These reports are systematically collected and provide broad coverage of regions that are commonly underrepresented in existing impact datasets. Using large language models, we extract qualitative and quantitative information on a wide range of non-monetary impacts at national and sub-national scales. The resulting dataset documents socio-economic impacts of natural hazards on the population, infrastructure and economy with a spatial detail reaching the subregional level. This resource is designed to support research and applications that require geographically explicit information on socio-economic impacts of disasters, enabling more precise and inclusive analyses of socio-economic consequences of natural hazards worldwide.

title: A Figure-Text Pair Dataset from Map-related Literature for Multimodal Model Research
abstract: High-quality multimodal datasets are essential for developing vision-language models, yet publicly available figure-text resources in specialized scientific domains remain limited. To address this gap, we present a large-scale figure-text pair dataset constructed from map-related scientific literature (FTPD-ML). The dataset was derived from 96,859 scientific publications in cartography, geography, remote sensing, and related disciplines, and provides 75,702 publicly redistributable figure-text pairs under Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY) licenses with multiple levels of textual representations, including original figure captions, standardized caption variants, and contextual paragraph descriptions, together with bibliographic metadata. To ensure compliance with copyright and licensing requirements, records from non-redistributable publications are represented by metadata only. The dataset supports a range of multimodal research tasks, including image-text retrieval, image captioning, scientific document understanding, and cartography-oriented vision-language studies.

title: A comprehensive six-year (2015–2020) dataset of six daily ground-level air pollutant concentrations across China
abstract: Air pollution poses significant risks to public health and the environment, highlighting the need for long-term, spatially comprehensive air quality datasets. Here, we present a large-scale ground-based air pollutant dataset comprising 4,453,372 daily records from 2,040 monitoring stations across mainland China during 2015-2020. The dataset includes concentrations of six major air pollutants: ozone (O 3 ), carbon monoxide (CO), nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ), sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ), and particulate matter (PM 2.5 and PM 10 ). To address missing observations in long-term monitoring records, we applied a LightGBM-based imputation framework that integrates model selection, feature enrichment, and iterative imputation to leverage spatiotemporal dependencies and inter-pollutant relationships. Each record is enriched with 128 features, including meteorological variables, remote sensing products, geographic attributes, anthropogenic indicators, and temporal descriptors.Comprehensive technical validation demonstrates that the reconstructed dataset preserves realistic temporal dynamics, spatial patterns, statistical distributions, and inter-pollutant correlation structures without introducing systematic biases. Benchmark experiments further illustrate the dataset’s usability for air pollution prediction tasks. This dataset is designed with machine-learning readiness, providing a comprehensive, high-quality, and standardized resource with spatiotemporally explicit data to advance air quality research, develop and benchmark machine learning models, conduct exposure assessment, and enable data-driven environmental management across China.

title: AI-Refined Ensemble Precipitation and Temperature Projections for Regional Impact Assessment over the Conterminous United States
abstract: Access to high-resolution long-term earth system projections is essential for advancing research in hydrology, agriculture, disaster management, and adaptation planning. This Data Descriptor presents an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-refined ensemble of Earth system model (ESM) projections for the conterminous United States at 1/24° (~4 km) spatial resolution. The dataset was generated by downscaling ten Coupled Models Intercomparison Project phase 6 (CMIP6) Earth system models (ESMs) under two emissions scenarios (SSP245 and SSP585) for an 80-year period (1980–2059). Two AI-driven methods, Super-Resolution Convolutional Neural Networks (SRCNN) and Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Networks (SRGAN), were applied to produce high-resolution daily precipitation and minimum/maximum temperature. This descriptor documents the input datasets, processing workflow, bias-correction steps, file structure, variables, spatial and temporal coverage, and technical validation of the released data. Validation analyses compare the generated products with Daymet observations and existing downscaled datasets to characterize spatial patterns, biases, temporal consistency, and differences among products. The dataset provides daily high-resolution historical and future earth system projections that can support regional, impact assessment, and related applications, and details the AI downscaling framework, training protocols, and evaluation strategies to ensure reproducibility and usability.

title: Unveiling hidden seismicity: An AI-derived catalog of 380k earthquakes for Sichuan Province, China
abstract: Long-term, high-resolution seismic monitoring is a prerequisite for characterizing seismic structures, delineating fault geometry, and mitigating earthquake risks. Located on the eastern margin of the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau, Sichuan Province is among the most seismically active regions in China, with particularly intense activity concentrated in the shale gas extraction zones of the southern Sichuan Basin. However, conventional manual earthquake catalogs are often incomplete with respect to microseismic events, limiting detailed seismological research. In this study, we constructed and released a high-resolution earthquake catalog for the Sichuan Province ranging from January 2019 to December 2020. Using continuous waveform data from 261 seismic stations, we adopted a deep learning-based workflow that involved phase picking, followed by event association and absolute location constrained by a high-resolution regional 3-D velocity model. The resulting catalog comprises 380,886 seismic events, approximately 5 times the number reported in the standard manual catalog for the same period. Completeness magnitude improved substantially, decreasing from M L 1.0 in the manual catalog to M L 0.1 in our catalog. This dataset provides a high-quality basis for subsequent studies in seismic activity analysis, seismic tomography, and hazard assessment.

title: Coarse grained molecular dynamics dataset of cyclic peptide interactions with lipid membranes
abstract: A large, standardized dataset of coarse grained molecular dynamics simulations is presented to characterize the interaction of cyclic peptides with an anionic lipid membrane under controlled conditions. The dataset comprises more than 10,000 trajectories generated using a chirality aware force field designed for cyclic peptide nanotubes and includes 3,855 peptide sequences simulated with identical protocols. Over 1,000 structural and energetic descriptors were extracted from each trajectory, quantifying peptide membrane contacts, interaction energies, and conformational variability. These descriptors provide mechanistically interpretable features that extend beyond sequence information and enable systematic comparison of membrane interaction behaviors across a chemically diverse peptide space. Example analyses demonstrate how the dataset supports unsupervised characterization of interaction profiles and the development of machine learning models that predict membrane behavior from coarse grained structure, illustrating its reuse potential for computational design and mechanistic studies of membrane active cyclic peptides.

title: Cesarean Scar Defect Segmentation in Transvaginal Ultrasound Images: a Dataset and Benchmark
abstract: Cesarean Scar Defect (CSD) is one of the most prevalent complications following cesarean delivery. Transvaginal ultrasonography is widely used for primary CSD screening. Accurate determination of CSD outline and dimensions is crucial for treatment. However, CSDs are frequently overlooked by sonographers due to small size and irregular morphology, suboptimal image quality, and limited clinical awareness in resource-constrained settings. Despite artificial intelligence advances in medical imaging, no public dataset exists for transvaginal ultrasound CSD segmentation. To address this gap, we present a comprehensive CSD dataset derived from 186 diagnosed patients, comprising 1,111 images and 16 videos, ultimately yielding 501 positive samples of confirmed CSD with precise pixel-level manual annotations. Annotations are performed following standardized clinical guidelines through collaboration between experienced sonographers and trained PhD students. This work provides high-quality benchmark resources for advancing medical image segmentation algorithms and promoting clinical innovation. Ultimately, improved CSD diagnosis and subsequent treatment strategies can enhance the quality of life in women of reproductive age, representing significant value for both medical research and clinical practice.

title: ToxiFruit: A Multi-class Image Dataset for Formalin Adulteration Detection in Fruits
abstract: The unauthorized use of formalin preservatives to delay ripening and extend shelf life of fruits remains a critical food safety concern, particularly in regions with limited routine monitoring. To support computer vision and machine learning research on adulteration detection, we present ToxiFruit , a curated multi-class image dataset focused on formaldehyde adulteration in fruits. The dataset contains 7,200 original images evenly distributed across eight classes, covering four commonly consumed fruits in Bangladesh (apple, malta, mango, and banana) captured in two conditions: fresh and formalin-treated. Images were collected under natural lighting across four geographically distinct locations in Bangladesh, introducing real-world variation in illumination, background, and fruit appearance. To support model development and benchmarking, four augmented derivatives were generated from each original image, producing 28,800 augmented images and 36,000 image files when combined with the 7,200 original images. All images were standardized to 224 × 224 pixels. HCHO-related sensor responses were measured for both fresh-control and formalin-treated samples using the same sensor module, while label consistency was further assessed through independent expert inspection. ToxiFruit provides a practical benchmark resource for developing, evaluating, and deploying automated fruit adulteration detection and food safety monitoring systems.

title: A Multimodal RGB-D Dataset of Visuo-Gestural Facial Expressions in Peruvian Sign Language
abstract: Peruvian Sign Language (LSP) is used by approximately 8,790 deaf individuals in Peru, yet computational resources for automatic sign language recognition remain critically limited. Visuo-Gestural Facial Expressions (VGFEs) convey essential grammatical and semantic information in sign languages, but existing datasets focus predominantly on manual gestures, neglecting these non-manual components that are fundamental for linguistic interpretation. We present SIGNO-PERU-FER, a multimodal dataset of dynamic VGFEs in Peruvian Sign Language. The dataset comprises 1256 synchronized RGB-D video sequences from 16 native LSP signers performing 14 Visuo-Gestural Facial Expressions categories selected for their visual similarity and classification challenges. Each sequence includes RGB video (1920 × 1080, 30 fps), depth maps (512 × 512), and 468 3D facial landmark points. Each recorded sequence was captured using an Azure Kinect DK device in controlled laboratory conditions with uniform lighting. Baseline recognition benchmarks are provided to support reuse and to characterize the technical difficulty of minimal pairs of VGFEs in LSP. The dataset supports research on sign language technologies, multimodal facial behavior modeling, and inclusive AI systems.

title: Large-scale, Stratified, Fully Annotated Acoustic Forest Soundscape Dataset of Avian Vocalizations from Eastern North America
abstract: Global environmental change is altering biodiversity through shifts in phenology, population dynamics, and animal behavior, creating a need for rapid, scalable approaches to monitoring biological communities. Passive Acoustic Monitoring (PAM) offers a powerful and scalable approach for assessing biodiversity and detecting changes in animal communities. Recent advances in deep learning methods have accelerated automated analysis of PAM data, yet progress is constrained by the limited availability of large, high-quality, strongly annotated datasets for training and evaluation. Here, we present a curated collection of three large-scale, multi-species datasets of avian vocalizations recorded using PAM across four forested landscapes in the northeastern United States. The collection comprises 217 hours of audio with expert-generated labelled annotations for ~183,000 vocalizations across 88 bird species. We provide open access to raw audio recordings, annotation files, and detailed metadata describing recording locations and sampling context. These datasets are designed to support the development, benchmarking, and validation of automated species detection and classification algorithms, while also enabling ecological analyses of species occurrence, activity patterns, and acoustic behavior. This strongly labelled acoustic data is intended to facilitate reproducible, cross-disciplinary research at the intersection of bioacoustics, ecology, and deep learning.

title: The Vienna 4G/5G Drive-Test Dataset
abstract: Machine learning for mobile network analysis, planning, and optimization is often limited by the lack of large, comprehensive real-world datasets. This paper introduces the Vienna 4G/5G Drive-Test Dataset, a city-scale open dataset of georeferenced Long Term Evolution (LTE) and 5G New Radio (NR) measurements collected across Vienna, Austria. The dataset combines passive wideband scanner observations with active handset logs, providing complementary network-side and user-side views of deployed radio access networks. The measurements cover diverse urban and suburban settings and are aligned with time and location information to support consistent evaluation. For a representative subset of base stations (BSs), we provide inferred deployment descriptors, including estimated BS locations, sector azimuths, and antenna heights. The release further includes high-resolution building and terrain models, enabling geometry-conditioned learning and calibration of deterministic approaches such as ray tracing. To facilitate practical reuse, the data are organized into scanner, handset, estimated cell information, and city-model components, and the accompanying documentation describes the available fields and intended joins between them. The dataset enables reproducible benchmarking across environment-aware learning, propagation modeling, coverage analysis, and ray-tracing calibration workflows.

title: A continental-scale dataset of ground beetles with high-resolution images and validated morphological trait measurements
abstract: Despite the ecological significance of invertebrates, global trait databases remain heavily biased toward vertebrates and plants, limiting comprehensive ecological analyses of high-diversity groups like ground beetles. Ground beetles ( Coleoptera: Carabidae ) serve as critical bioindicators of ecosystem health, providing valuable insights into biodiversity shifts driven by environmental changes. While the National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON) maintains an extensive collection of carabid specimens from across the United States, these primarily exist as physical collections, restricting widespread research access and large-scale analysis. To address these gaps, we present a multimodal dataset digitizing over 13,200 NEON carabids from 30 sites spanning the continental US and Hawaii through high-resolution imaging, enabling broader access and computational analysis. The dataset includes human-made measurements of elytra length and width of each specimen image, establishing a foundation for automated trait extraction using AI. High correlations between measurements made by humans from images to those taken by humans on physical specimens ensure reliability for ecological and computational studies. By addressing invertebrate under-representation in trait databases, this work supports AI-driven tools for trait-based research, fostering advancements in biodiversity monitoring and conservation.

title: A multi-period dataset of retrogressive thaw slump susceptibility for Northern Hemisphere permafrost regions
abstract: Permafrost thaw accelerates the initiation and expansion of retrogressive thaw slumps (RTSs), with critical implications for the terrestrial carbon cycle and land-surface energy budgets. However, long-term datasets characterizing spatiotemporal variations in RTS susceptibility across Northern Hemisphere permafrost regions remain lacking. Here, we integrate 55,673 georeferenced RTS occurrence records with machine learning models to generate a 1-km spatiotemporal dataset of RTS susceptibility from 2000 to 2100 under multiple climate change scenarios. RTS susceptibility is defined as the relative occurrence probability of RTS under specified environmental conditions. We independently modelled RTS susceptibility for the Arctic and Tibetan Plateau and merged the individual outputs to construct a spatially harmonized dataset for the Northern Hemisphere. Model performance was evaluated using standard classification metrics, yielding mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.96 ± 0.005. The dataset includes georeferenced RTS inventories and gridded susceptibility maps for the entire Northern Hemisphere permafrost domain, covering the baseline period and diverse future climate scenarios. These products provide a foundational resource for quantifying permafrost hazard risks, infrastructure exposure, and carbon-climate feedbacks under climate warming.

title: Synchronized Vibration Data Collection for Fault Diagnosis of Induction Motors under Varying Rotating Speeds and Loading Conditions
abstract: This paper presents a vibration dataset for fault diagnosis of three-phase induction motors operating at variable speeds, controlled by a Siemens S7–1500 programmable logic controller (PLC) and an INVT GD20-1R5G-S2 variable-frequency drive (VFD). The dataset captures triaxial vibration signals from two ADXL355 accelerometers mounted at the bearing housing and motor frame, acquired at a sampling rate of 4 kHz using a Teensy 4.1 microcontroller. Data were collected across five operating speeds (varying from 10 to 50 Hz in steps of 10 Hz) and two mechanical load conditions (5 kg load and no-load), covering six fault scenarios: normal condition, mechanical looseness, horizontal shaft misalignment at 3 mm and 5 mm, and vertical shaft misalignment at 3 mm and 5 mm. The complete dataset comprises 60 CSV files totaling 1.72 GB, each containing six vibration channels and a numerical fault label. Technical validation was performed through time-domain and frequency-domain signal analysis, followed by machine learning classification using Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) classifiers, achieving accuracies of 99.79%, 96.73%, and 92.96%, respectively, across 12 fault classes. These results confirm the dataset’s suitability as a benchmark for rotating machinery fault diagnosis research, with potential applications in machine learning, deep learning, and cross-speed generalization fault detection methodologies.

title: Benchmark Dataset of Vibrational Signals for Artificial Intelligence Applications in Mechanical Systems
abstract: This study introduces a benchmark dataset of 7,000 vibration signals from a modular mechanical transmission system, simulating real-world setups with artificially induced faults in gears, V-belts, and roller chains. Data were collected under various configurations, capturing fault propagation across interconnected modules and including both healthy and faulty states. Time- and frequency-domain analyses reveal distinct vibrational patterns under fault conditions. To assess diagnostic complexity, classic unsupervised fault detection models, using statistical features and deep learning autoencoders, were applied. Low clustering accuracy and poor label alignment highlighted the difficulty of detecting subtle anomalies without supervision. The dataset’s variability and realism offer a robust resource for advancing signal processing using machine learning and deep learning in condition monitoring. This work provides a scalable, diverse, and diagnostically rich dataset, addressing gaps in existing resources that often focus on isolated components and lack fault diversity, and supports research in unsupervised learning, representation learning, and predictive maintenance within Industry 4.0.

title: LLM Board Game Tournaments: A Dataset of Moves, Validity, and Reasoning
abstract: We present A Dataset of LLM Strategic Play , comprising 9,572 tournament records from a controlled eight-round Swiss-system tournament involving 20 LLMs across four board games: Tic-Tac-Toe, Connect Four, and their goal-inverted variants, Suicide and Not Connect Four. Move records include the model identity, board state, legal moves, observed latency, and textual justification. Moves are validated with a GDL-based arbiter and a rectification protocol that allows up to 10 retries. Overall, 25.2% of LLM-generated moves are invalid, approximately 50% in Suicide; in total, 106 game sequences ended in automatic forfeit, represented by terminal records in the dataset. Even the best-performing model records an invalid-move rate of 10.7%, showing that rule-following errors remain present under these evaluation conditions. These observations illustrate the use of simple board games as controlled domains for evaluating LLM behavior, where strategic decision-making can be examined together with compliance with formal constraints. The proposed pipeline–GDL-based validation, Swiss tournament design, and rectification protocol–is domain-agnostic and can be extended to other GGP settings, supporting scalable evaluation of LLM decision-making under formal rules.

title: Steady-State Visual-Evoked EEG Dataset for Visual Function Assessment via Biomarker Extraction
abstract: Amblyopia and intermittent exotropia (IXT) are prevalent pediatric visual impairments characterized by deficits in cortical visual processing. Understanding the underlying neurophysiological mechanisms and tracking neural recovery requires high–quality, objective data, yet open–access EEG datasets specifically designed for these pediatric populations—particularly those with a longitudinal dimension—remain scarce. Here, we present the steady–state visual–evoked EEG (S2VEEG) dataset, a 64–channel electroencephalography (EEG) dataset collected from pediatric participants, including amblyopia, IXT, and healthy controls. The S2VEEG dataset uses a multimodal experimental paradigm comprising resting–state recordings, transient Visual Evoked Potentials (VEP), and Steady–State Visual Evoked Potentials (SSVEP). The dataset employs a longitudinal design, capturing neural activity both at baseline and following therapeutic interventions (perceptual learning for amblyopia and strabismus surgery for IXT). For technical validation, differential entropy (DE) and small–worldness properties are extracted as features and analyzed using Support Vector Machine (SVM), Residual Graph Convolutional Broad Network (RGCB), and Emotion Transformer (EmT) classifiers. The classification performance suggests that the recorded EEG signals contain discriminative electrophysiological information across visual function states, thereby supporting the usability of the S2VEEG dataset as candidate discriminative measures for methodological development and exploratory analyses. These results are intended as a technical validation of data quality and feature separability, while this resource provides a valuable platform for future studies investigating brain–eye interactions, treatment–induced neuroplasticity, and the development of objective biomarkers for monitoring visual function recovery.

title: Dataset for Glycemic Control Analysis in Type 1 Diabetes under Multiple Daily Injection Treatment in Free-living Conditions
abstract: Open-source datasets of glucose monitoring play a critical role in facilitating research in diabetes management and treatment, while allowing the development of Artificial Intelligence models for blood glucose forecasting. While many efforts are spent on patients with Type 1 Diabetes with Continuous Glucose Monitoring, many patients are still relying on Multiple Daily Injection treatment due to lower cost and easier accessibility. Due to individual differences in living styles and physiological responses to various insulin treatments, more structured datasets with detailed behavioral and physiological factors in real-life living conditions are expected. Contributing to the research on Type 1 Diabetes, this study introduces the OU-DATASET, a longitudinal, multimodal resource for analyzing glycemic control within multiple daily injection treatment. The dataset includes glucose level monitoring, insulin injection, activity tracker data (heart rate, steps) records, and self-reported lifestyle events (meals, exercise, stress) collected from 22 participants on multiple daily injection therapy over an 8-week period. This descriptor details the data collection protocol, data architecture, and accessibility of the dataset. The OU-DATASET supports further development of data-driven algorithms and models for the treatment management of Type 1 diabetes.

title: A Global Dataset of Surface NO2 Estimation Based on Machine Learning Using Process-based Information
abstract: Nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) is a key air pollutant associated with numerous adverse human and environmental health outcomes, yet globally consistent, fine-resolution long-term surface NO 2 datasets remain scarce due to the shortcomings of available data sources and the complex relationships between emissions and surface NO 2 concentrations. Here, we improve estimates of global monthly surface NO 2 concentrations at fine spatial resolution (0.01° × 0.01°) over 2005–2023 by developing, optimizing, and applying a highly efficient gradient boosting decision tree (LightGBM) framework underpinned with multi-source datasets, including geophysical process-based a priori information that leverages simulations with the GEOS-Chem chemical transport model, road‐network metrics, land‐cover features, and other relevant environmental predictors over 2005–2023. Evaluated against 9,913 ground monitors across 66 countries, the machine learning model achieves significant agreement for the benchmark year 2023 with 10-fold spatial cross-validation for monthly surface NO 2 estimates ( \({R}^{2}\) = 0.82, RMSE = 2.34 ppb, slope = 0.97), and similar long-term performance over 2005–2023 ( \({R}^{2}\) = 0.76, RMSE = 3.42 ppb, slope = 0.97). We apply Buffered Leave Isolated Sites and Clusters Out (BLISCO) spatial cross-validation to rigorously account for spatial autocorrelation, finding that traditional spatial cross-validation overestimates performance over unmonitored areas and that process-based physical and chemical information from chemical transport model (GEOS-Chem) simulations significantly improves R 2 by 20% globally. Global per-pixel uncertainty quantification indicates that this dataset provides NO 2 estimates with median relative uncertainty of 35% and absolute uncertainty of 1.81 ppb. This 19-year fine-resolution global NO 2 dataset with a consistent methodology, process-based information, rigorous validation and uncertainty quantification offers a valuable resource for quantifying the magnitude, spatial patterns, long-term trends and impacts of global NO 2 exposure.

title: A national fish pond dataset for Nigeria generated using automated detection and segmentation
abstract: Fish and other aquatic foods are a vital source of nutrients and livelihoods around the world, and with the stagnation of capture fisheries, countries have increasingly turned to aquaculture. While the geographic expansion of aquaculture is evident from national statistics, much less is known about subnational patterns of growth. Notably, the spatial extent of smallholder aquaculture ponds is poorly understood, limiting our ability to ask basic questions about local risks and benefits stemming from aquaculture investments. To begin to address this, we develop a national dataset of open-air fish pond boundaries for Nigeria using an open-source automated segmentation pipeline to systematically delineate individual fish ponds. As Africa’s most populous nation and third-largest fish producer, Nigeria plays a crucial role in regional food security. With its diversity of geographies and fish production systems, Nigeria offers the ideal case for developing automated approaches to fine-scale fish pond mapping. First, we use georeferenced point labels of fish pond locations to manually delineate fish pond boundaries and create a labeled dataset (N = 14,021). Combining these labels with high-resolution satellite imagery, we then train a national segmentation model and perform predictions across the entire country (precision: 86.3%; recall: 87.9%). We then train a post-processing random forest classifier to distinguish fish ponds from false positives (overall F1: 96.9%, with a per-state F1 mean of 63.5 ± 36.8%). Applying this approach, we identify a total of 246,786 fish ponds throughout Nigeria. Our scalable approach offers a flexible means for fine-scale tracking of smallholder aquaculture patterns, potentially applicable across other smallholder-dominated geographies. Such data are central for food system monitoring and informing interventions to bolster smallholder productivity and market access.

title: A Cyber-Attack Detection Dataset for Distribution Systems Generated from a Scaled Cyber-Physical Testbed
abstract: Modern power distribution systems, characterized by deep integration with communication networks, are increasingly susceptible to cyber threats. A critical challenge for attack detection research lies in the scarcity of authentic datasets derived from physical hardware testbeds. To address this critical need, an open dataset, termed CPDS-AD, is established for cyber-attack detection in cyber-physical distribution systems. This dataset is generated utilizing a developed laboratory-level scaled testbed, which emulates the steady-state operating and cyber-measurement processes of a 13-node three-phase unbalanced medium-voltage-type radial distribution feeder and a three-layer cyber architecture. It captures both normal-operation data and data recorded under various realistic cyber-attacks, including multiple types of false data injection and denial-of-service attacks. Raw communication messages are meticulously recorded and processed into synchronized, time-aligned measurement data. The quality and effectiveness of the dataset for developing data-driven attack detection methods are demonstrated through technical validation, employing dimensionality reduction and unsupervised machine learning models.

title: High-resolution European soil property maps based on LUCAS and AlphaEarth Foundations satellite embeddings
abstract: High-resolution soil property maps have a wide range of applications, e.g. policymaking and precision agriculture. Previously published maps covering the EU-27 plus the UK range in resolution from 250 to 30 metres depending on the soil property. In this work, we produced 10 m resolution maps for soil texture (clay, silt, sand), coarse fragments, pH and bulk density. They are the products of a machine-learning workflow trained on LUCAS soil datasets and using AlphaEarth Foundations satellite embeddings as predictors. We performed hyperparameter tuning and training on Random Forests (RF) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). The best-performing models were ANN, with R 2 values ranging from 0.21 for coarse to 0.69 for pH. The best-performing ANN hyperparameters for each soil property were used to produce soil property maps over Europe as well as uncertainty estimate maps obtained from Monte Carlo dropout. The generated maps aim to close the resolution gap for the EU-27 + UK and provide a promising baseline for precision agriculture, soil health assessment at field scale and spatial planning.

title: A Dataset for Visual Detection of Litchi Fruit Borer Infestation and Anthracnose
abstract: The litchi industry has long been severely plagued by the litchi fruit borer ( Conopomorpha sinensis ) and litchi anthracnose ( Colletotrichum gloeosporioides ). Despite the rapid development of deep learning in agricultural monitoring, there is currently no public dataset that supports the simultaneous detection of these two stresses, let alone a systematic simulation of variable lighting conditions in real postharvest environments. To address this issue, we constructed LitchiPestDisease—the first multi-illumination image dataset dedicated to the detection of litchi fruit borer infestation and litchi anthracnose. This dataset contains images collected from the core production areas in Maoming, Guangdong, China, during 2024 and 2025. To support the simulation of realistic grading scenarios, the dataset includes the original images and three systematically enhanced illumination variants (front lighting, back lighting, and side lighting) generated following the protocol described in this paper. All these images are provided in the public repository. The pest subset includes 3,061 original images, all annotated with bounding boxes for borer damage holes. The disease subset consists of 3,644 original images, a portion of which are additionally annotated with polygon instance segmentation, where each lesion is labeled by its severity (mild, moderate, severe). The corresponding enhanced images under three lighting conditions are fully provided in the public repository. Benchmark experiments based on YOLOv12n validated the effectiveness of the dataset: severe anthracnose detection reached near-perfect mAP50 levels, while pest detection achieved an mAP50 of 0.6539 under mixed lighting conditions. Comparative analyses across different lighting conditions and disease severity levels revealed the robustness and limitations of the model (e.g., the recall rate for mild disease under side lighting dropped to 0.878). Furthermore, benchmark experiments on instance segmentation revealed the performance variation of segmentation models under different lighting conditions, jointly providing a multi-task evaluation benchmark for algorithm optimization. LitchiPestDisease provides an important benchmark resource for the intelligent detection of fruit quality in real-world scenarios.

title: A Comprehensive Multimodal Gait Dataset for Lower-Limb Wearable Robotics in Indoor and Outdoor Environments
abstract: Daily walking locomotion exhibits variability, asymmetry and ground constraints. Recording and analyzing real-world locomotion data is essential for expanding the application scenarios of wearable robots such as exoskeletons and prostheses. However, most existing gait datasets are collected with specialized equipment under predefined laboratory conditions, lacking visual information from natural walking environments and annotations for transitional states across different surfaces. To address this problem, we collected walking data from 17 healthy participants across diverse indoor and outdoor environments, including kinematic data from seven inertial measurement units (IMUs), foot pressure data from force sensing resistors (FSRs) with 96 points, and visual data from three front-facing cameras with 1280 × 720 resolution. All modalities are time-synchronized, with 448 clips and 243607 data frames in total. Full annotations are provided, covering 16 classes of lower-limb locomotion states (8 steady states, 8 transitional states), bilateral gait phases and bilateral coordinates of the center of pressure (COP). This dataset can be utilized for exploring the applications of machine learning in locomotion state recognition and intelligent control of lower-limb wearable robotics.

title: A Labelled Dataset of Healthy and Diseased Maize from Tanzania
abstract: Early detection of crop diseases is essential for improving maize productivity and strengthening food security, particularly in regions where agriculture is the main source of livelihood. This paper presents a labelled image dataset of healthy and diseased maize leaves collected in Tanzania to support the development of machine learning models for crop disease diagnosis. The dataset includes data on: healthy leaves, and diseased leaves of Maize Lethal Necrosis (MLN) and Maize Streak Virus (MSV) which are among the most significant threats to maize production in the country. All images are annotated to support tasks such as image classification, object detection and image segmentation. The dataset comprises a total of 243,539 labelled images covering multi-season, making it one of the largest publicly available maize image datasets from Tanzania. It serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners advancing artificial intelligence applications in agriculture.

title: A spatially and temporally aligned contrast-non-contrast cardiac CT dataset of pigs
abstract: Traditionally, cardiac CT imaging relies on the use of contrast agents. However, in some cases such agents cannot be used, and there is a need to develop novel AI-based algorithms to accurately segment cardiac structures from CT images, recorded without the use of contrast agents. To address this challenging problem, we have collected a spatially and temporally aligned cardiac CT dataset of pigs with and without the use of contrast fluid. This dataset consists of 10 different pigs, CT-scanned multiple times between 15 and 130 kg to cover a wide set of body weights. A subset of the dataset is manually labelled, to enable development of supervised learning-based segmentation techniques.

title: Grid2Text Dataset Aligning Meteorological Grid Data with Expert Reasoning Chains
abstract: Accurate meteorological forecasting is fundamental to public safety and economic stability, but it heavily relies on numerical weather prediction (NWP) models, whose complex outputs are often inaccessible to non-experts. Although large language models (LLMs) show potential in translating structured data into natural language to automate forecast reporting, progress has been constrained by a critical scarcity of datasets that bridge the modality gap and capture the implicit reasoning of human experts. To address this, we present Grid2Text , a rigorously developed dataset aligning ERA5 meteorological grid features with expert-verified textual forecasts, encompassing explicit reasoning chains for temperature trends, wind vector transitions, humidity ranges, and precipitation types. Furthermore, we establish validation benchmarks derived from a human-in-the-loop workflow to ensure the physical consistency and logical accuracy of the data. We anticipate that this open-access dataset will catalyze the development of interpretable LLM approaches for weather forecast discussions, ultimately advancing the field of scientific text generation.

title: Refined annotations of intrahepatic portal and hepatic veins from thin-slice CT images
abstract: Accurate segmentation of intrahepatic vessels in contrast-enhanced CT is limited by spatial resolution, variable contrast timing, and the complexity of peripheral vascular anatomy. Public datasets such as the Medical Segmentation Decathlon Task 08 include annotations of hepatic structures but provide incomplete delineation of small-caliber portal and hepatic veins. This work describes HVA-CT (Hepatic Venous Annotations CT), a dataset derived from the contrast-enhanced thin-slice CT volumes of the Medical Segmentation Decathlon Task 08, in which intrahepatic venous structures were re-annotated with more complete anatomical delineation. The dataset comprises refined three-dimensional segmentations of portal and hepatic venous systems generated through a structured workflow combining baseline model outputs, AI-assisted vessel branch identification, and expert review. For each case, updated venous segmentation masks, liver segmentations, and a standardized tool for intrahepatic vessel extraction are provided. The dataset is intended to support the development and evaluation of automated methods for hepatic vessel segmentation and analysis.

title: A Synchronous EEG-fNIRS Motor Execution and Imagery Dataset
abstract: In the field of motor imagery brain-computer interfaces (MI-BCI), researchers have developed multimodal BCI systems that leverage the complementary spatiotemporal characteristics of electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). This integration has been shown to substantially improve the accuracy and robustness of decoding movement intentions. However, publicly available synchronous EEG-fNIRS datasets for motor imagery tasks remain scarce. Such scarcity severely constrains the development of multimodal fusion algorithms. To address this gap, we introduce and openly release the Synchronous EEG-fNIRS Motor Execution and Imagery Dataset (SEFMEID), a concurrent hybrid EEG-fNIRS motor imagery dataset collected from 50 healthy participants. The dataset includes resting baseline, left-right hand motor execution (ME), and left-right hand motor imagery (MI) conditions, with each subject performing 25 trials for the right task and 25 trials for the left task. We also provide single-modality and multimodal classification results, as well as neurovascular coupling analyses, to validate the usability and quality of the dataset. In the deep learning results, the multimodal fusion algorithm achieves an improvement of approximately 10% over the best-performing unimodal approach. The public release of SEFMEID aims to serve as a valuable resource for advancing multimodal MI-BCI algorithms, investigating neurovascular coupling mechanisms underlying motor imagery, and accelerating clinical translation in neurological rehabilitation.

title: An observation-based daily gridded precipitation dataset for forecast verification
abstract: As numerous artificial intelligence (AI)-based weather forecasting models are trained by climate reanalysis, there is an urgent need for independent observation-based datasets for forecast verification. Mainly based on the Global Historical Climatology Network (GHCN), this paper develops the GHCN daily gridded precipitation (GHCNdgp) dataset, covering the period from 2020 to 2025. Specifically, two daily station-based observation datasets–GHCN daily and Global Surface Summary of the Day–and three subdaily datasets–GHCN hourly, Integrated Surface Database and Integrated Global Land surface Dataset–are integrated to enhance global station density and spatial coverage. The spatiotemporal consistency checks are combined with integrity and reporting time checks to identify anomalous observations and infer stations’ reporting times. Furthermore, the GHCNdgp is compared against three existing precipitation products using Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC), i.e., the Integrated Multi-satellitE Retrievals for Global Precipitation Measurement (IMERG) V07 Late, the Multi-Source Weighted-Ensemble Precipitation (MSWEP) V2.8 and the Global Precipitation Climatology Centre (GPCC) First Guess Daily product. The results show that more than 90% of the anomalous observations come from identical values and duplicate sequences. The median PCC for stations with daily accumulation periods shifted by 24 hours is generally below 0.25. The quality control checks improve the median PCC from 0.46 to 0.62 under the IMERG, from 0.54 to 0.71 under the MSWEP and from 0.33 to 0.47 under the GPCC. These findings indicate that the GHCNdgp dataset effectively mitigates mismatches in observation reporting times and aligns with the grid resolution of 0.25° × 0.25° common in AI weather forecasts. This dataset is publicly available on Zenodo in the Network Common Data Form format, providing essential ground-truth precipitation observations specifically for benchmarking AI weather forecasts.

title: Beyond built-up land: Mapping complete settlement footprint in China from 1990 to 2020 with Landsat imagery
abstract: Accurate mapping of human settlements is vital for understanding urbanization, human-environment interactions, and sustainable development. Existing medium-resolution products often underestimate the real spatial extent of settlements by focusing solely on built-up cores. Here, we present the China Settlement Footprint 1990–2020 (CSF30) dataset, a nationwide product depicting complete human settlement footprints from Landsat imagery at five-year intervals. CSF30 was generated using an Entity-Based Image Analysis framework integrated with a deep learning architecture. To ensure spatio-temporal generalizability and boundary accuracy, the model was trained via a two-stage strategy utilizing a built-up area dataset and a newly annotated settlement footprint dataset. Comprehensive validation demonstrates that CSF30 achieves a mean F1-score of 0.91 across the 30-year period, showing distinct advantages in representing rural and peri-urban areas compared to existing products. CSF30 provides a critical, high-quality baseline for diverse applications, including investigating settlement trajectories, assessing ecological and environmental impacts, and monitoring progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

title: High-resolution dataset of core needle prostate biopsies with expert pathologist annotations
abstract: We present an expert-labelled image dataset designed to support automated analysis of image-guided prostate core needle biopsies (CNBs) in the context of prostate cancer diagnosis. The dataset includes 37 whole slide images (WSIs), corresponding to 60 CNBs stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E), from 32 patients. The dataset contains 15480 manual expert annotations, covering benign glands, tumor, stromal tissue, adipose tissue, nerves, nerve ganglia, blood vessels, muscle, and inflammatory cells. Additional recorded features include stromal retractions, normal and abnormal glandular secretions, and tissue or digital image artifacts. These annotations represent the normal findings that pathologists encounter in routine diagnosis. The annotations were performed by two experienced uropathologists with final labels determined by consensus; immunohistochemical techniques were used as guidance. This dataset provides a foundation for training and benchmarking machine learning models for prostate biopsy assessment and is openly available to facilitate reproducibility and further research.

title: Vineyard RGB-D, LiDAR and GNSS/RTK datasets for grapevine segmentation and localisation to enable autonomous robotic pruning
abstract: Agricultural robotics is becoming increasingly relevant for executing arduous tasks where human labour is scarce. Grapevine pruning is a seasonal task that, when performed manually, requires a worker to perform selective cutting of the grapevine canes. For a robot to conduct this type of task autonomously, it needs to navigate the vineyard rows without colliding with the grapevines, as well as retain information regarding each grapevine to perform the operation. This work presents datasets collected in a vineyard, comprising RGB and depth images, LiDAR and GNSS/RTK data, acquired using both a handheld device and a mobile robot. Furthermore, 494 RGB images obtained from the handheld device recordings were annotated with segmentation masks in YOLO format. The datasets support the development and evaluation of computer vision, localisation, mapping and sensor fusion algorithms for autonomous robots. Technical validation demonstrates the consistency and usability of the annotated data for training deep learning models.

title: A high-resolution global flood susceptibility dataset derived from multi-source earth observation and geospatial data
abstract: Floods are among the most damaging disasters worldwide, necessitating high-resolution modeling of where terrain and environmental conditions predispose societies to flooding. While geospatial data are invaluable for flood susceptibility mapping, comprehensive and globally consistent datasets remain scarce. We present the Global Flood Susceptibility Map (GFSM v1), a globally harmonized 30 m flood susceptibility dataset produced by incorporating multi-source flood conditioning factors accounting for topographic, hydrological, meteorological, and anthropogenic characteristics within a machine learning framework. A gradient-boosted tree model was trained on ~17,000 curated grid tiles with ~30.45 million training samples, using a global flood inundation dataset as training labels and nine conditioning factors (elevation, slope, aspect, wetness index, vegetation index, height above nearest drainage, water/roads proximity, and rainfall frequency). The model was deployed based on geopolitical and climate strata (units n = 192) to generate global pixel-level susceptibility. Rigorous cross-validation indicates strong model predictive accuracy (median area-under-curve ~0.95), and the output captures localized flood-prone regions worldwide. GFSM v1 offers a global open-source, high-resolution resource to support informed flood risk management, particularly in data-sparse regions.

title: CTX-UXO: Contextual visual dataset for localisation, classification and identification of unexploded ordnance
abstract: Unexploded Ordnances (UXOs) are explosive weapons that failed to detonate during deployment, posing significant threats to civilian safety and post-conflict recovery. The Contextual Vision for Unexploded Ordnances (CTX-UXO) dataset addresses this challenge by providing 3520 high-resolution RGB images, median size 2124 px square, containing UXOs collected over four years across all seasons and weather conditions. The dataset encompasses 15 449 annotated instances labeled as UXOs, with twelve subcategories for identification tasks, in which mortar bombs, projectiles and grenades constitute the predominant classes, supporting systems research and development in UXO classification, detection, instance segmentation and related applications, and providing multiple labelling formats such as YOLO and COCO. For the detection task including binary classification, an end-to-end solution for training, validation and testing is available as a reference by presenting a neural network optimized for edge deployment, Faster-RCNN with MobileNet V3 backbone, deployed for real-time inference with reduced costs on Nvidia Jetson Orin, achieving up to 23 frames per second with 62.18% Ap50 for UXO localisation and binary classification.

title: Long-term seasonal ruminant livestock distribution datasets in China’s grazing production systems
abstract: Accurate spatial distribution data of grazing livestock are essential for rangeland management and sustainability assessments, yet existing global datasets lack production system differentiation and seasonal resolution. We present China’s Long-term Ruminant Livestock Distribution in Grazing Livestock Production Systems (CLRD-GLPS) dataset, providing seasonally resolved distributions of cattle, sheep, and goats across China’s grazing systems from 2000 to 2021. The dataset was generated using a stacking ensemble machine learning framework integrating Random Forest, XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, and Extra Trees, combined with interpretable machine learning for livestock segmentation. CLRD-GLPS includes 1-km resolution gridded maps distinguishing warm-season and cold-season distributions, with CV-based model-uncertainty layers. Model validation on independent test data achieved R 2 values of 0.954–0.961 for cattle and 0.896–0.915 for sheep/goats. External validation at city level yielded R 2 of 0.74–0.81, supporting dataset reliability across spatial scales. The dataset addresses critical gaps in livestock distribution mapping by separating grazing from non-grazing systems and capturing seasonal dynamics, supporting applications in forage-livestock balance assessment, climate impact studies, and evidence-based policy development.

title: A Pan-European Multimodal Dataset Linking Field Photos with Satellite Image Time Series for Agricultural Mapping
abstract: AgroFusion is a continental-scale, multimodal, pixel-based reference dataset designed to support rigorous evaluation and reproducible research in agricultural remote sensing and geospatial Artificial Intelligence (AI). Built upon the 2018 and 2022 Land Use/Cover Area frame statistical Survey (LUCAS), the dataset integrates 211,483 field observations (107,642 in 2018 and 103,841 in 2022), each linked to field photos (four cardinal views, point centered view, and a close-up), LUCAS land-cover and land-use annotations, with monthly pixel-based Satellite Image Time Series (SITS) from Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1, and Landsat-8, agrometeorological data from ERA5-Land, topography from the Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, soil properties from AI4SoilHealth, and annual embeddings from AlphaEarth geo-foundation model. AgroFusion is the first continental-scale resource for pairing geo-tagged field photos with pixel-based SITS, semantically rich agricultural covariates, and precomputed foundation model embeddings. This combination will enable a wide range of applications, including multimodal and multiscale crop type classification and phenology retrieval, and the interpretation of satellite-derived agricultural products using ground-level visual context.

title: A curated comprehensive dataset of asymmetric organocatalytic Mannich reaction
abstract: The asymmetric organocatalytic Mannich reaction is one of the key methods for constructing chiral β-aminocarbonyl moieties that occur in the structures of many biologically active compounds, including drugs. The selection of a catalyst and reaction conditions that ensure high enantioselectivity for specific substrates remains a largely empirical task. The scarcity of structured, openly available data hinders the application of machine-learning methods to enantioselectivity prediction and rational catalyst design. We present a dataset of 4015 reactions manually extracted from 153 publications spanning 2000–2025 and covering 468 unique organocatalysts. The structures of the reagents and catalysts, the reaction conditions, and the target values ( ee , ΔΔG‡) are provided in a machine-readable form suitable for training AI-models.

title: Renewable generation and electricity consumption datasets for energy market models generated with artificial intelligence
abstract: Analysis of future energy scenarios requires comprehensive and reliable input datasets. Open-access datasets increase transparency and reduce barriers to entry in modeling. In our study, we use artificial neural network models to transform 43 years of weather reanalysis data into hourly resolution, nationwide time series of renewable energy production (solar, onshore and offshore wind) and electricity consumption datasets. During our research, we developed a data quality control procedure for the ENTSO-E hourly-resolution database based on heat maps, histograms, and z-score values, thereby ensuring that our artificial intelligence models learn from high-quality data. Modeling was performed for all European countries with sufficient data quantity and quality to train machine learning models. The proposed neural-network-based database combines the widest spatial coverage among the reviewed datasets with accuracy that in most cases exceeds existing solar, wind, and electricity consumption databases, making it a valuable complement for European electricity system modelling. The open-access data series created can be used directly as input data for electricity market models, e.g., in unit commitment, network load distribution and pricing studies, and are also particularly suitable for analyzing the frequency, duration, and regional overlap of periods of low renewable energy production (Dunkelflaute events).

title: PRIME-CVD: Paired Synthetic Cohort and Structured EMR-Style Data Assets for Education in Cardiovascular Risk Modelling
abstract: In recent years, progress in medical informatics and machine learning has been accelerated by the availability of openly accessible benchmark datasets. However, patient-level electronic medical record (EMR) data are rarely available for teaching or methodological development due to privacy, governance, and re-identification risks. This has limited opportunities for students from healthcare and clinical backgrounds to gain hands-on experience in coding, data management, and cardiovascular risk modelling. Here we introduce PRIME-CVD, a parametrically rendered informatics medical environment designed explicitly for medical education. PRIME-CVD comprises two openly accessible synthetic data assets, each representing 50,000 adults undergoing primary prevention for cardiovascular disease and parameterised to reproduce the statistical characteristics of a derivation cohort from the Australian New South Wales Lumos linked-data resource. The datasets are generated entirely from a user-specified causal directed acyclic graph parameterised using characteristics of the reference cohort, publicly available Australian population statistics and published epidemiologic effect estimates, rather than from patient-level EMR data or trained generative models. Data Asset 1 provides a clean, analysis-ready cohort suitable for teaching exploratory analysis, stratification, statistical coding, and survival modelling, while Data Asset 2 systematically transforms the same cohort into a structured relational, EMR-style database with deliberately introduced data-quality challenges, including missingness, heterogeneous terminology, inconsistent measurement units, and cross-table linkage requirements. Together, these complementary assets enable healthcare and clinical learners to develop practical skills in coding, data cleaning, harmonisation, cohort reconstruction, and cardiovascular risk modelling without exposing sensitive information. Because all individuals and events are generated de novo, PRIME-CVD preserves realistic subgroup imbalance and risk gradients while ensuring negligible disclosure risk. Although the released PRIME-CVD cohort represents adults with no prior history of cardiovascular disease undergoing primary-prevention risk assessment, the complete data-assembly pipeline is provided through the dedicated GitHub repository. Educators may adapt the supplied code, parameters, and data-generating assumptions to construct alternative synthetic cohorts suited to their own teaching objectives. PRIME-CVD is released under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence to support reproducible and scalable health data science education.

title: Nationwide annual agricultural land-use maps of Germany from 1990 to 2023 derived from satellite imagery
abstract: We present German-wide annual agricultural land-use maps from 1990 to 2023, created from Landsat and Sentinel-2 images using a deep learning approach. Based on farmers’ declarations from 2006 to 2022, we extracted annual training samples for 13 crop classes and one grassland class. These samples were used to train a multi-year one-dimensional convolutional neural network, which was subsequently applied to generate the annual land-use maps. Between 2010 and 2022, overall map accuracies ranged between 85% and 93%. When averaged over time, dominant classes like grassland, rapeseed, winter cereals, sugar beet, and maize were detected with high accuracy (≥90%). Conversely, minor classes such as fallow land and plantation were predicted with low accuracy (≤52%). Comparison of map areas with agricultural statistics over time revealed high correlations for most classes, particularly maize ( r = 0.978). The presented maps provide an essential basis for analyzing long-term trends in agricultural land-use. They can be used to fill temporal gaps in national agricultural statistics and to disaggregate those statistics to higher spatial units.

title: A Multi-Center, Multi-Modal Chest CT and Clinical Dataset for Differentiating Pulmonary Aspergillus from Non-Aspergillus and Non-Fungal Infections
abstract: Pulmonary Aspergillus infection (PAI) presents a critical diagnostic challenge due to its clinical management differing significantly from that of pulmonary non- Aspergillus fungal infection (PNAFI) and pulmonary non-fungal infection (PNFI). While Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a promising solution for rapid triage, its development is currently severely bottlenecked by data scarcity. Existing studies primarily rely on small, private, and single-center datasets, which hampers the generalizability of models and precludes reproducible research. To date, there is no publicly available, multi-center benchmark dataset that integrates imaging with key host immune factors for this domain. To address this critical gap, we present the first comprehensive, open-access dataset of its kind, collected from 569 patients across 4 hospitals in China. This dataset comprises: (1) standardized volumetric chest CT scans in NIfTI format; (2) a curated clinical record containing definitive diagnostic labels, demographics, and critical laboratory variables (e.g., lymphocyte counts, D-dimer). Technical validation was conducted for two binary tasks: Task 1, Fungi vs Non-Fungi, and Task 2, Aspergillus vs non- Aspergillus . This study introduced three models for classification: a clinical model using clinical variables, an imaging model based on CT images, and a fusion model combining both clinical variables and CT images. Model performance was evaluated through receiver operating characteristic analysis, with sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and area under the curve (AUC) reported as key metrics. As a rare and versatile resource, this dataset supports not only the development of robust AI classification algorithms but also facilitates clinical prediction modeling, the investigation of the predictive role of host variables (e.g., age, comorbidities), decision-making regarding invasive interventions, and radiological education, thereby accelerating precision medicine in pulmonary infectious diseases.

title: A paediatric dataset of non-dermoscopic skin images for dermatological AI research
abstract: This paper introduces DermoPed, a non-dermoscopic dermatology dataset composed almost entirely of paediatric patients’ images. The long-term goal is to advance research in automated dermatological image analysis with a specific focus on non-dermoscopic images, i.e., those captured using consumer-grade cameras, thereby promoting accessible diagnosis for underprivileged and underserved populations. However, this objective is often challenged by the limited availability of data and the heterogeneous quality of clinical images, issues that are discussed in detail in this work and carefully addressed during the preprocessing phase. The resulting dataset comprises more than 46,000 medium-to-high quality images from 229 distinct patients, the majority of whom are paediatric. In addition, we release a separate “challenging” subset of lower-quality crops with automatically computed image-quality labels, intended to support the study of model robustness under realistic acquisition conditions.

title: An fMRI dataset of verbalized spontaneous thought with annotated transcripts and self-report trait measures
abstract: Spontaneous thought is pervasive in everyday human cognition, yet datasets capturing its neural dynamics under minimally interrupted conditions remain limited. The current dataset was acquired from a think-aloud functional MRI experiment in which 118 participants continuously verbalized their spontaneous thoughts during 10-minute scanning sessions. The raw MRI data and verbal transcripts with sentence-level timestamps were previously released and analyzed in our prior study examining neural activity associated with thought transitions. Building on that release, we additionally provide preprocessed MRI data, speech transcriptions with word-level timestamps aligned to image acquisition, large language model-generated ratings of transcribed thoughts across emotional and sensory dimensions, and self-report survey measures assessing personality, mental health, and cognitive abilities. Validation analyses demonstrated activation in expected cortical regions associated with speech production and sensory content identified from transcript annotations, agreement between language model and human ratings, and adequate internal consistency of survey measures, supporting the dataset’s overall quality. This dataset enables reuse for investigations of spontaneous thought, speech generation, and individual differences using naturalistic functional MRI data.
